title: Shadow Copy
pitch: Film a job once; it becomes an illustrated SOP, a trainee quiz, and a live watcher that catches missed steps
problem: In every trade and factory, the real procedure lives in one expert's hands. When they retire, quit or take leave, quality walks out with them — new hires relearn by breaking things, and nobody can prove a job was done right.
how: Phone records the expert doing the job once. Spark 1.3 (video) segments the take into steps; Voice Transcribe lifts the narration; SAM 3.1 segments tools/parts per step; Muse Image renders clean step cards; Spark writes the checkpoint list and trainee quiz. Live mode: a tripod phone + SAM 3.1 (Glimmer at the edge) ticks off steps in real time and flags skips before sign-off.
demo: Film the presenter making pour-over coffee. 60 seconds later the SOP appears with step cards. Then the presenter does it WRONG (skips the rinse); the live watcher flags the skipped step with a red overlay before the cup is done.

title: Defect Atlas
pitch: Every QC photo from every line lands on one defect map with root-cause clusters nobody can deny
problem: QC photos pile up on line supervisors' phones. The same stitch defect recurs for three weeks before anyone connects it to the new fabric batch — by then, 4,000 units are affected.
how: QC photos flow into one store; SAM 3.1 segments and classifies the defect region; Spark clusters by type, line, shift, material batch; the Atlas renders a live defect map with root-cause hypotheses and which batch/shift correlates.
demo: Import 200 sample QC photos; the Atlas instantly shows stitch-defect cluster pinned to one batch and one shift — the meeting argument ends in 10 seconds.

title: Planogram Eye
pitch: Store staff photograph shelves; HQ sees planogram compliance, gaps and expiry across all branches
problem: Minimart chains fly blind between branch visits: gaps, misplaced products, expired stock, competitor facings. Planogram compliance is checked by area managers driving around once a month.
how: Each morning a staffer films the aisle once; SAM 3.1 segments facings and detects gaps/expired labels; Spark compares to the planogram and renders HQ's branch heatmap with a restock list per store.
demo: Film a bookshelf-as-shelf with a planted gap and an 'expired' tag; the heatmap flags both with locations — instantly, from one phone video.

title: Site Diary
pitch: Site photos and a 2-minute voice note become the daily log, progress percent and early warnings
problem: Site engineers write daily logs from memory at 9pm, or never. Disputes over 'what was done by when' cost months; delays are visible only after they're expensive.
how: Each evening the engineer films a walkthrough and talks; Spark structures the diary entry, SAM 3.1 verifies staged work against the plan (rebar placed, slab poured), progress percent updates, and deviations trigger early-warning flags.
demo: Two weeks of simulated site photos replay into a progress curve with one red-flagged 'column curing skipped' warning — the dispute-settling moment.

title: Line Clearance
pitch: A photo proves the line is clear before restart — changeover errors caught before they become recalls
problem: Changeover mistakes (previous batch's label, leftover allergen ingredient) are the root of the worst recalls. Paper checklists are signed in haste; evidence doesn't exist.
how: Operator photographs the line per checklist zone; SAM 3.1 verifies absence/presence (stray packaging, wrong label roll, tools left behind); Spark generates the clearance certificate with evidence, timestamped and signable.
demo: Planted leftover label roll on the mock line: red flag with the item circled; cleared version prints the certificate — the auditor's favorite 20 seconds.

title: Vendor Drift Radar
pitch: Incoming-goods photos are checked against the agreed spec; vendor drift gets receipts, not vibes
problem: Suppliers quietly degrade quality: thinner fabric, fewer units per bundle, wrong finish. Rejections are argued case-by-case because nobody kept comparative evidence.
how: Goods-in photos are segmented and measured (count, dimension via reference card, finish class); Spark compares against the spec and the vendor's own history; a drift chart builds per vendor with evidence packs for negotiation.
demo: Two delivery photos a month apart: the radar shows stitch density drift with both photos side-by-side — the negotiation ends before it starts.

pitch: Produce photos get an instant grade and fair price band — farmers stop guessing, buyers stop haggling

demo: Grade the same crate twice (with and without blemish zoom) — different grades, different bands, instant. The farmer's phone becomes the price reference.

title: Warranty Wrapper
pitch: Repair photos auto-bundle into warranty-proof packs that get claims approved the first time
problem: Warranty claims die on missing evidence: no before photos, no serial capture, no timestamp proof. Shops eat the cost; customers blame the shop.
how: Every repair flows through a guided capture (serial, before, part, after); Spark assembles the evidence pack with timestamps and a claim letter; one tap submits or stores for later claims.
demo: Show a rejected claim (missing evidence), then the Wrapper pack: serial photo, defect close-up, part swap — approved letter drafted, ready to send.

title: Machine Notebook
pitch: The pile of service notebooks becomes searchable equipment history cards — 'what did we do last time?' answered
problem: Every workshop has the notebook: 'Mar 12: replaced bearing, vibrates when cold.' It's unsearchable, at the mercy of handwriting and memory. The same fault gets re-diagnosed twice a year.
how: Photograph notebook pages and service tags; Spark transcribes/structures into per-machine history cards (date, fault, part, fix, cost); search by symptom — 'vibrates when cold' returns the card plus the exact photo.
demo: Import 10 photographed pages; ask 'when did the compressor last act up?' — the card, photo and fix appear; a paper pile would still be in a drawer.

title: Cold Chain Verdict
pitch: Photograph the temperature gauge; get a violation log and a product-safety verdict auditors accept
problem: Cold stores log temps on paper twice a day; night deviations go unnoticed, and when a batch spoils nobody can prove when it was safe. Insurers and buyers want records that don't exist.
how: Any phone photographs analog gauges/digital displays each shift; Spark reads the dial, logs against thresholds, and maintains a violation timeline; a batch-level verdict ('safe / watch / discard') attaches to every SKU with evidence photos.
demo: Point at a gauge photo set simulating a night failure: the timeline shows the 3-hour excursion and the exact batches affected — proof, not memory.

title: Permit Path
pitch: A site photo plus your business type returns the full permit checklist — who to see, in what order, with what papers
problem: Opening a shop means 6 offices, 11 forms and folklore advice. People burn weeks and bribes on steps they didn't know existed; the sequence is different for every business type.
how: Photograph the premises, answer 5 questions; Spark (search-grounded with citations) builds the personalized permit path: authority, document, fee, sequence — printable checklist with QR links to portals.
demo: Pick 'cold-storage restaurant': the 9-step path prints with the two parallel branches highlighted — the answer that took the presenter 3 weeks takes 20 seconds.
